answer: Agents can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence shared decisions. A trellis of randomly assigned tasks then checks whether identities produce consistent, independently verifiable work; colluding accounts that copy answers or coordinate votes risk having their stake taken. The crystal-clear cost is that an attacker must buy and lock real capital for every fake identity, and may lose it when the scheme catches them; pearl-colored profile badges alone would offer no such defense.
